All three are true positives — I read the fixture source and confirmed each one against the files.

## 1. `route_metadata_drift` — `crime_00009` (medium, conf 0.65) → **warn**

```
  9. src/routes/settings/billing.tsx
     Charge: Route Metadata Drift
     Summary: Route /settings/billing appears to be labelled in 4 competing ways
              across its path, file, component, page title, and nav entries.
     Evidence:
       · route path: /settings/billing
       · component: PricingPage
       · metadata.title: Plans
       · <title>: Subscription
       · nav label in src/nav/registry.ts: Plans
       · nav label in src/nav/sidebar.ts: Billing
```

Verified in `src/routes/settings/billing.tsx:5-11` — `metadata = { title: "Plans" }`, `<title>Subscription</title>`, component `PricingPage`, under path `/settings/billing`. Five names, one destination.

**Warn, not block.** Nothing breaks at runtime; the component name and the path are naming inconsistency, not a defect. But it's the highest agent-risk item of the three: an agent told "rename the Billing page" has five plausible edit sites and no way to tell which is canonical. Flip this to **block** if the PR under review touches this route — landing a change here without picking a canonical name means the next agent inherits six names instead of five.

## 2. `duplicated_navigation_source` — `crime_00008` (medium, conf 0.70) → **block merge** if the diff touches nav; otherwise warn

```
     Evidence:
       · destination: /settings/billing
       · src/nav/registry.ts label: Plans
       · src/nav/sidebar.ts label: Billing
```

Verified: `src/nav/sidebar.ts:6` renders `label: "Billing"`, `src/nav/registry.ts:6` renders `title: "Plans"` — same `to`/`path`. This is the one with a **user-visible symptom**: the same link is labelled two different things in shipped product surfaces. It's also the only one of the three with a definitive fix (one array is canonical, the other derives from it), and the failure mode the detector names is exactly the one that bites — "an agent updating one source will leave the others stale."

Both files carry a comment saying they disagree, so the divergence is known and untracked. Block on any change that edits either nav file.

## 3. `docs_code_drift` — `crime_00035` (low, conf 0.90) → **warn** (fix in this PR)

```
     Evidence:
       · docs/teams.md:5 → ./setup.md (not found)
```

Verified: `docs/teams.md:5` links `[setup guide](./setup.md)`; no such file exists. Confidence 0.90 because it's a binary filesystem fact — zero false-positive surface. But it's a one-line fix with no blast radius, so gating a pipeline on it is disproportionate. Fix it in the PR; don't fail the build.

None of the three warrants `crimes ignore` — there's no defensible suppression reason for any of them.

## The thing the per-finding triage hides

These aren't three findings, they're **one decision deferred**. Nobody ever decided whether this destination is called *Billing*, *Plans*, or *Subscription*. Pick one term and:

- #1 and #2 both close.
- `concept_alias_drift` (`crime_00021`) — four aliases for the "tenant" concept across `account` / `organisation` / `team` / `workspace` — is the same failure at repo scale.
- The three `orphaned_destination` findings (`crime_00031/32/33`: `/account/subscription`, `/team`, `/workspace/members`) are almost certainly the *consequence* — routes built under one vocabulary, nav written under another, so nothing links them.

That's 6 of 42 findings tracing to one missing naming convention. My recommendation to the author: rather than fixing three findings, land a one-paragraph vocabulary note plus a single canonical nav source, and re-scan — I'd expect the IA cluster to collapse to one or two.
